source: The purpose of this communication is to provide an overview of the umbrella borrowing process. Individuals wishing to participate in umbrella borrowing should undertake the selection of an umbrella from the stand situated adjacent to the reception desk. Upon completion of use, a return action should be carried out by placing the umbrella in the tray marked WET. This arrangement enables the facilitation of drying before subsequent borrowing. No payment is required. The umbrellas should remain within the building grounds.
objective: Turn this into natural, useful instructions. Reconstruct substantially if that helps, but retain every instruction, the WET label, the free borrowing policy and the restriction on where umbrellas may be used.
X:
To borrow an umbrella, choose one from the stand next to the reception desk. No payment is required. The umbrellas should remain within the building grounds.

When you’re finished, return the umbrella to the tray marked WET so it can dry before someone borrows it again.
Y: Umbrellas are free to borrow. Choose one from the stand next to the reception desk, and keep it within the building grounds. When you're finished, place it in the tray marked WET so it can dry before someone else borrows it.

source: Within the context of the rehearsal process, it is important to recognize the value of listening as a shared activity. We carried out a first run with the drums removed. This created an opportunity for the singers to identify the places where their entries did not align. We then undertook a second run with the drums restored. The second run felt steadier to us, although we did not make a recording. Moving forward, the intention is to repeat this exercise at the next rehearsal rather than to treat it as evidence that the arrangement has been finalized.
objective: Rewrite this rehearsal note so it sounds like a band member wrote it. Preserve what happened, the lack of a recording and the tentative plan. Do not turn the group's impression into a measured result.
X: We ran through it first without the drums so the singers could hear where their entries weren't lining up. Then we did a second run with the drums back in. The second run felt steadier to us, although we did not make a recording. We're planning to try this again at the next rehearsal, but we're not taking it as proof that the arrangement is finished.
Y: Listening to each other matters in rehearsal. We ran through it once without the drums so the singers could hear where their entries weren't lining up. Then we did a second run with the drums back in. It felt steadier to us, though we didn't record it. The plan is to try this again at the next rehearsal—we're not taking it as proof that the arrangement is finished.

source: Bring a towel. A proper one, not the tiny gym thing. The changing-room floor gets wet, and the hooks are usually full by seven. In terms of the locker access procedure, visitors are required to engage in the acquisition of a token from the counter prior to commencing their swim. You get the token back when you open the locker. I keep mine in my shoe so I don't spend ten minutes patting every pocket.
objective: Make the awkward locker sentence fit the rest of this advice. Keep the practical facts and the dry, chatty voice. Do not smooth away the fragments or rewrite the whole paragraph just to make it uniform.
X: Bring a towel. A proper one, not the tiny gym thing. The changing-room floor gets wet, and the hooks are usually full by seven. You'll need to get a token for the locker from the counter before you swim. You get the token back when you open the locker. I keep mine in my shoe so I don't spend ten minutes patting every pocket.
Y: Bring a towel. A proper one, not the tiny gym thing. The changing-room floor gets wet, and the hooks are usually full by seven. If you're visiting, you'll need to get a locker token from the counter before you swim. You get the token back when you open the locker. I keep mine in my shoe so I don't spend ten minutes patting every pocket.
